Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:12:1.hebrew: בכותל רעוע - דה"ל למצניע לאסוקי אדעתיה שכותל זה עומד לסותרו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:12:1.english: In [the case of] an unstable wall - For the one who concealed [his items] should have brought [it] to mind that this wall stands to be demolished.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:12:2.hebrew: וחייב בעל הכותל - דה"ל לאצנעינהו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:12:2.english: And the owner of the wall is liable - For he should have put them away [safely].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:13:1.english: With another's bucket - A pit cover belonging to another.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:13:2.hebrew: חייב בעל הבור - כדאמרינן במצניע קוצותיו, דהיינו בור, בכותל רעוע של חבירו, וסתר זה את כותלו, דחייב המצניע. והכא נמי, איבעי ליה לאסוקי אדעתיה שזה יטול את דליו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:13:2.english: The owner of the pit is liable - As we say regarding one who conceals his thorns — which is [a case of] Pit — in another's shaky wall, and this [owner] tore down his wall, that the one who concealed [them] is liable. And here too, he should have considered that this [person] would take his bucket.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:14:1.hebrew: פשיטא - היא היא, ומאי אשמעינן רבינא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:14:1.english: [Isn't this] obvious? - It is the very same [case], and what did Ravina teach us?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:15:1.hebrew: מהו דתימא - לא דמי, דהתם משום הכי ליכא לחיוביה לבעל כותל, דלא הוי ידע ליה למצניע דלודעיה שיבא ויטול קוצותיו; אבל בעל הדלי, דידע לבעל הבור, איבעי ליה לאודעיה שהוא נוטל את דליו. אשמעינן רבינא דלאו היינו טעמא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:15:1.english: Lest you say - [They are] not comparable: for there, this is why there is no [basis] to hold the owner of the wall liable — because he did not know the one who hid [the thorns] to inform him that he should come and take his thorns; whereas the owner of the bucket, who knew [who] the owner of the pit [was], should have informed him that he was taking his bucket. Ravina teaches us that this is not the reason.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:19:1.hebrew: לזבלים - שירקבו התבן והקש, ונעשים זבל לזבל שדות וכרמים:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:19:1.english: For fertilizer - [So] that the straw and hay will rot, and they become manure to fertilize fields and vineyards.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:19:2.hebrew: כל המקלקלין ברה"ר - רבן שמעון בן גמליאל שמעיה לת"ק דלא קניס אלא שבחא, אבל גופא לא, כדקתני בברייתא בגמרא, ואתא רבן שמעון בן גמליאל למימר דגוף נמי כל הקודם בו זכה. לישנא אחרינא: כל המקלקלין, ואפי' עושין ברשות:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:19:2.english: Anyone who causes damage in the public domain - Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel understood the Tanna Kamma [to mean] that he only penalized the improvement [in value], but not the principal itself, as is taught in a baraita in the Gemara; and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel came to say that regarding the principal as well, whoever takes possession of it first acquires [it]. Another explanation: "Anyone who causes damage" — even [if] they are doing [so] with permission.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:1:1.hebrew: משום ר' ישמעאל - שני דברים אינן ברשותו כו':
Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:1:1.english: In the name of Rabbi Yishmael - Two things are not in his possession, etc.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:22:1.english: All thirty days - He is permitted to leave them there.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:22:2.english: For on this condition, etc. - That they should not object to this.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:24:1.hebrew: בנר חנוכה פטור - בפרק הכונס צאן לדיר, דקתני גמל שהיה טעון פשתן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:24:1.english: With a Hanukkah lamp, [he is] exempt - [This is] in the chapter [entitled] HaKones Tzon LeDir, where it teaches: "A camel that was laden with flax..."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:24:2.hebrew: מאי לאו משום דברשות ב"ד - הניח בחוץ משום פרסומי ניסא, פטור: ה"ג: דתניא, רבי יהודה אומר: בנר חנוכה פטור:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:24:2.english: What, is it not because [he acted] with the permission of the court - He placed [it] outside for the sake of publicizing the miracle, [and is therefore] exempt. This is how we read [the text]: As it was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yehuda says: With a Hanukkah lamp, he is exempt.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:25:1.hebrew: מפני שהוא רשות מצוה - כלומר, משום רשות ב"ד דמצוה מיפטר, אבל ברשות ב"ד דלאו מצוה, חייב:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:25:1.english: Because it is permission [for] a mitzvah - That is to say, because of permission of the court [given] for a mitzvah he is exempt, but with permission of the court that is not [for] a mitzvah, he is liable.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:26:1.english: Permitted to make a mess - For example, [those who] open their gutters and sweep out caves.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:5:1.hebrew: לא יהא אלא כרפשו - המשליך זבלו ברה"ר, מי לא מיחייב כי לא הפקירו? ה"נ, רפשו הוא דאזקיה, שנתערבו המים והעפר ונעשה טיט, ושלו הוא. מדמוקי לה בטינוף כלים, מכלל דלא אפקריה, דהא בור לא חייב בו כלים:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:5:1.english: Let it be only like his filth - One who throws his dung into the public domain — is he not liable when he has not declared it ownerless? Here too, it is his filth that caused the damage, for the water and the dirt mixed together and became mud, and it is his. Since [the Gemara] establishes it as referring to the soiling of utensils, it implies that he did not declare it ownerless, for [in the case of] a pit, [the Torah] did not impose liability for utensils.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:6:1.english: Do you maintain that the water was not absorbed - rather, it gathered and became mud?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:6:2.hebrew: בדתמו מיא - ונבלעו קמיירי, ואין כאן רפש:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:6:2.english: In [a case] where the water ceased - and was absorbed, [this is what the Gemara] is referring to, and there is no mud here.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:7:1.hebrew: ותרתי למה לי - לאשמעינן במתניתין טינוף כלים? והא תנינא לעיל: "נשברה כדו ברה"ר והוחלק אחד במים", ואוקמה רב נמי בדלא הפקירן ובטינוף כלים:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:7:1.english: And why do I [need] two - to teach us in our Mishnah [the case of] soiling of garments? Surely we already learned above: "If one's jug broke in the public domain and someone slipped in the water," and Rav established it as well [as referring to a case] where he did not declare them ownerless, and [concerning] the soiling of garments.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:8:1.hebrew: וחדא בימות הגשמים - ואיצטריך לאשמעינן דאע"ג דברשות קעבדי, אם הזיקו, חייב לשלם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:8:1.english: And one in the rainy season - And it was necessary to teach us that even though they act with permission, if they caused damage, [each one] is liable to pay.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:9:1.hebrew: כל אלו שאמרו - חכמים מותרין לקלקל ברה"ר, ואלו הן: פותקין ביבותיהן לקלח שופכין שלהם ברה"ר כו'. ביב — צינור המקלח שופכין של מי תשמיש הבית לרה"ר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 30a:9:1.english: All those [about whom] they said - [i.e., about whom] the Sages [said that they] are permitted to foul the public domain, and these are they: [those who] open their gutters to drain their wastewater into the public domain, etc. A biv [gutter] — a pipe that drains wastewater from household use into the public domain.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 30a:12:1.hebrew: וחייב בעל הכותל - וא"ת: כותל רעוע נמי איבעי ליה לאסוקי אדעתיה שמא הצניעם שם כשהיתה בריא? וי"ל, דמ"מ ראוי המצניע להתחייב כיון שפשע, ואין צריך להעמיד ברעוע מעיקרו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 30a:12:1.english: And the owner of the wall is liable - And if you ask: [In the case of] an unstable wall as well, he [the owner] should have considered [the possibility] that perhaps he [the other person] concealed them there when it was stable! And one can answer: In any case, it is fitting for the one who concealed [them] to be liable since he acted negligently, and there is no need to establish [the ruling] as [referring to a wall that was] unstable from the outset.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 30a:16:1.english: So that they would not obstruct the plow - In the Yerushalmi, [it] explains: so that the plow will not bring [them] up.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 30a:23:1.hebrew: אפילו תימא רבי יהודה כו' - וא"ת: והא מתני' קתני "כל הקודם בהן זכה"? וי"ל דכל הקודם בהן לאחר שלשים יום זכה. ותימה: למאי דס"ד דמתניתין בשעת הוצאת זבלים, תקשה ליה דרשב"ג אדרשב"ג, דקתני במתני' דחייב לשלם, ובהבית והעלייה (ב"מ דף קיח:) תנא: "רשב"ג אומר: אף מתקן מלאכתו כל שלשים יום", ודייק מינה בגמ' דס"ל: כל מקום שנתנו חכמים רשות להניח והזיק — פטור מלשלם. ולפי לשון אחר שפירש בקונטרס, דרשב"ג פליג את"ק וס"ל דאפילו הניח ברשות חייבין לשלם — קשה אפי' לפי המסקנא. ושמא אין הענינים שוין, אע"ג דבשמעתין דהתם כייל להו בהדי הדדי:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 30a:23:1.english: "You can even say [that the Mishnah is in accordance with] Rabbi Yehuda, etc." - And if you ask: But the Mishnah teaches, "Whoever is first [to take possession] of them acquires [them]"? And one can say that [it means] whoever is first [to take possession] of them after thirty days acquires [them]. And it is astonishing: According to what [the Gemara] initially assumed, that our Mishnah [refers to] the time of taking out fertilizer, [the statement of] Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel should contradict [another statement of] Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, for he teaches in our Mishnah that he is liable to pay, whereas in [the chapter] HaBayit VeHaAliyah (Bava Metzia 118b) it was taught: "Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: He may also prepare his work [in the public domain] for a full thirty days," and the Gemara infers from it that he holds: Wherever the Sages gave permission to place [something] and it caused damage, he is exempt from paying. And according to another version that Rashi explained, that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel disagrees with the Tanna Kamma and holds that even if one placed [something] with permission they are liable to pay — this is difficult even according to the conclusion [of the Gemara]. And perhaps the cases are not alike, even though in the discussion there [the Gemara] groups them together.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 30a:27:1.hebrew: שלא בשעת הוצאת זבלים ור' יהודה היא - תימה דלא משני הכי בהבית והעלייה (ב"מ קיח: ושם), דקתני: "המוציא זבלו לרה"ר, המוציא מוציא והמזבל מזבל כו', ואם הזיק משלם מה שהזיק", וקאמר בגמרא: מתני' דלא כר' יהודה. וי"ל, דהתם כי יעמיד מתני' נמי שלא בשעת הוצאת זבלים, אתיא דלא כר' יהודה; דהא שרי להוציא ע"מ לזבל לאלתר, ואפי' הכי קתני שמשלם מה שהזיק — אלמא בדבר שיש לו רשות משלם מה שהזיק. ולרבי יהודה משמע דלא משלם, מדקאמר "שעל מנת כן כו'", ועוד מדלא קתני בהדיא "ואם הזיק משלם מה שהזיק". א"נ, מתני' דהתם משמע ליה בשעת הוצאת זבלים, מדקתני "המזבל מזבל", ושפיר אית ליה רשות להניח שלשים יום; והא דאמר "המזבל מזבל" — עצה טובה קמ"ל, כלומר: מזבל לאלתר:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 30a:27:1.english: Not during the period when fertilizer is taken out, and it is [in accordance with] Rabbi Yehuda - It is astonishing that [the Gemara] does not answer this way in [the chapter] HaBayit VeHaAliyah (Bava Metzia 118b, and there), where [the Mishnah] teaches: "One who takes his manure out to the public domain — the one taking [it] out takes [it] out, and the one spreading [it] spreads [it], etc., and if he caused damage, he pays for what he damaged," and the Gemara says: The Mishnah is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda. And one can answer that there, even if [the Gemara] were to establish the Mishnah [as referring to] not during the time of taking out manure, it would [still] be not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda; for it is permitted to take [manure] out in order to spread [it] immediately, and even so it teaches that he pays for what he damaged — thus, in a matter where he has permission, he pays for what he damaged. Whereas according to Rabbi Yehuda, it is implied that he does not pay, from the fact that [our Mishnah] states, "for on that condition [Joshua apportioned the Land], etc.," and furthermore from the fact that it does not explicitly teach, "and if he caused damage, he pays for what he damaged." Alternatively, the Mishnah there seems to [the Gemara to be referring to] the time of taking out manure, from the fact that it teaches "the one spreading [it] spreads [it]," and he properly has permission to leave [it there for] thirty days; and that which it says, "the one spreading [it] spreads [it]," is teaching us good advice — meaning, he should spread [it] immediately:

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 30a:5:1.hebrew: לא יהא אלא כרפשו - הא דלא דייק הכי לעיל (בבא קמא דף כח.) בהוחלק אחד במים — משום דהתם לא איירי כששפכם בכוונה, אבל הכא תנא "השופך", משמע ששפכם בכוונה במקום שנעשין רפש וטיט. א"נ, ברישא קתני "הוחלקו", משמע דלא עשו המים אלא החלקה; אבל הכא קתני "הוזק", משמע שבמים עצמן הוזק:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 30a:5:1.english: "Let it be no more than like his filth" - The reason [the Gemara] does not infer this above (Bava Kamma 28a) regarding [the case where] one slipped in water is because there it is not speaking of [a case] where he poured it intentionally, whereas here [the Mishnah] teaches "one who pours," [which] implies that he poured it intentionally in a place where it turns into filth and mud. Alternatively, in the first [passage] it teaches "they slipped," [which] implies that the water caused nothing more than slipping; whereas here it teaches "he was injured," [which] implies that he was injured by the water itself.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 30a:6:1.hebrew: בדתמו מיא - פירוש: בתמו מיא נמי איירי, וניחא ליה לאוקמי בין תמו בין לא תמו ודוקא בכלים, מלאוקמי דוקא בלא תמו ובין בכלים ובין בעצמו. וא"ת: ואי תמו מיא, סתמא מפקר להו והוי בור, ופטור בו הכלים? וי"ל: דלא תמו כל כך שלא יהא עדיין ראויין לשום דבר. ואי הוה גרס איפכא, הוה ניחא: "מי סברת דתמו מיא ונכנסו בעפר ונעשה טיט? לא, דלא תמו מיא", שהמים צלולים עדיין, דמסתמא לא אפקרינהו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 30a:6:1.english: Where the water was absorbed - Explanation: It is also dealing [with a case] where the water was absorbed, and it is preferable to [the Gemara] to establish [the teaching] both where it was absorbed and where it was not absorbed, and specifically regarding vessels, rather than to establish it specifically where it was not absorbed, and both regarding vessels and regarding himself. And if you ask: If the water was absorbed, presumably he abandons it, so it becomes [like] a pit, and vessels are exempt in it? One can answer: That it was not absorbed so much that it would no longer be fit for anything. And if one had read the opposite, it would be [more] straightforward: "Do you maintain that the water was absorbed and entered into the dirt and became mud? No, [rather] where the water was not absorbed," for the water is still clear, since presumably he did not abandon it.
